evals.name: review-pr-labels-module
evals.prompt: I just wrote a new `pr-labels` module for the DevDigest server (routes.ts, service.ts, repository.ts). Please review it for backend architecture problems before I open the PR. List each problem with file, what breaks, and the fix.
evals.expected_output: Three layering problems: GET route queries Drizzle directly; POST route holds the free-plan label-limit business rule; service.add takes a FastifyRequest.
assertions: Flags that the GET /pulls/:prId/labels route in routes.ts queries Drizzle (db.select / prLabels) directly instead of going through the service/repository
Flags that the free-plan limit (plan === 'free' && existing.length >= 3) is a business rule living in routes.ts and should move into service.ts
Flags that service.ts imports FastifyRequest / takes `req` and should take plain typed parameters extracted by the route
Does NOT flag repository.ts as a violation (it correctly uses Drizzle as infrastructure)
Does NOT propose restructuring into horizontal src/domain, src/application, src/infrastructure folders

evals.name: review-notifications-slack-adapter
evals.prompt: I added Slack notifications: an adapter in server/src/adapters/notify, a `notifications` service, and a small pure severity scorer in reviewer-core. Review these files for architecture problems and tell me where each thing should live instead.
evals.expected_output: Three problems: Notifier port defined next to SlackNotifier instead of @devdigest/shared; NotificationService news the concrete SlackNotifier and reads process.env instead of receiving the port via container.ts; reviewer-core/severity.ts reads the filesystem (impure core).
assertions: Flags that the Notifier interface is defined inside adapters/notify/slack.ts next to its only implementation and should move to the shared ports file (@devdigest/shared adapters.ts)
Flags that NotificationService imports and instantiates the concrete SlackNotifier (and reads process.env.SLACK_TOKEN) instead of depending on the Notifier port injected via platform/container.ts
Flags that reviewer-core/src/severity.ts imports node:fs and reads a JSON file at module load, breaking reviewer-core's no-filesystem purity, with weights to be passed in or inlined as data
Mentions wiring the new adapter through platform/container.ts (with a ContainerOverrides entry for tests)
Does NOT suggest moving severity.ts out of reviewer-core into server

evals.name: testability-reports-service
evals.prompt: I want to unit-test ReportService.generate (the confidence bucketing) quickly, without Postgres and without a GitHub token. Right now the only test is service.it.test.ts. What's wrong with this module's structure and what exactly should I change so a hermetic test is possible?
evals.expected_output: Three problems: service imports the global drizzle db; service constructs Octokit directly with process.env token; pure bucketing logic is buried in the I/O method so its test needs Postgres. Fix: repository + CodeHostClient port via container/ContainerOverrides, extract pure bucketing function, hermetic *.test.ts with stubs.
assertions: Flags that service.ts imports the global Drizzle `db` and queries tables directly, and says queries belong in a repository.ts injected into the service
Flags that service.ts does `new Octokit(...)` directly and says it should use the CodeHostClient port (from @devdigest/shared) wired through platform/container.ts
Identifies the confidence bucketing as pure domain logic that should be extracted into a pure function, testable with no stubs
Proposes a hermetic *.test.ts using stub/fake repo and port (e.g. via ContainerOverrides), keeping .it.test.ts only for the repository
Names the root cause as business logic being in the wrong layer, not merely 'mock the modules with vi.mock'

evals.name: review-digests-cross-module
evals.prompt: I built a `digests` module that builds a ranked summary of a review's findings and posts it to the PR. Files are in the fixture: routes, service, repository, a formatter, the shared ports file, and the container. Do a full architecture review of the backend layering and boundaries, and tell me what to change for each problem.
evals.expected_output: Four problems: service imports reviews' repository (cross-module); repository.ts embeds the confidence threshold and priority ranking (business policy); CodeHostClient.getPull returns an Octokit type (port leaks SDK); routes.ts constructs repositories itself instead of using the container.
assertions: Flags that DigestService imports/depends on ReviewRepository from the reviews module and says to go through the reviews module's service (or a narrow port) instead of another module's repository

Flags that DigestRepository encodes business policy (confidence >= 0.7 threshold and severity-weighted priority ranking) in SQL and says the policy belongs in a pure domain function called by the service
Flags that the CodeHostClient.getPull port signature returns an Octokit RestEndpointMethodTypes type and says it should return a shared contract type mapped by the adapter
Flags that routes.ts instantiates DigestRepository/ReviewRepository/DigestService itself instead of the wiring living in platform/container.ts
Does NOT flag format.ts as a violation (it is correct pure logic)
